storylines.label: Research Deep
storylines.latest_title: ScaffoldAgent: Utility-Guided Dynamic Outline Optimization for Open-Ended Deep Research

prior_narrative.tldr: Through mid-June, deep research agents kept getting redefined faster than they could be standardized. An arXiv paper argued that benchmarks only grade a single-shot report and miss whether an agent improves under feedback, and ran a multi-turn process-level evaluation. AWS then shipped a build pattern: an end-to-end competitive research agent on Deep Agents and Bedrock AgentCore with isolated multi-step execution. DRFLOW moved the target toward predicting a personalized, enterprise-style workflow rather than just a report, and the latest beat, ScaffoldAgent, attacks the long-form report itself — utility-guided dynamic outline optimization for open-ended deep research.
prior_narrative.whats_new: The newest item, ScaffoldAgent (Jun 18), shifts the focus from what to evaluate back to how to generate: it frames open-ended deep research as multi-round retrieval feeding a coherent long-form report, and makes the outline the optimization target with a utility-guided, dynamically optimized scaffold — a generation-side answer after a run of benchmark-side papers.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: How you evaluate and structure a deep research agent is still unsettled: report quality, improvement under process-level feedback, personalized workflow prediction, and outline-driven coherence are four different bars, and the one you pick changes what you build. AWS's Deep Agents + Bedrock AgentCore walkthrough is a ready reference for the multi-step plumbing under any of them.

status.detail: A fast-moving research thread where the success criterion for deep research agents keeps being redefined — evaluation, workflow prediction, and now report-generation structure.

beats.headline: Single-shot benchmarks miss whether agents improve under feedback
beats.summary: Reframes evaluation around multi-turn, process-level feedback rather than one-shot report scoring.

beats.headline: AWS ships an end-to-end research agent on Deep Agents + Bedrock AgentCore
beats.summary: Moves from critique to construction with isolated execution for multi-step workflows.

beats.headline: DRFLOW benchmarks personalized workflow prediction, not report generation
beats.summary: Argues enterprise work needs the agent to predict a personalized workflow, not just summarize.

beats.headline: ScaffoldAgent makes the outline the lever for long-form deep research
beats.summary: Utility-guided dynamic outline optimization for open-ended, multi-round-retrieval reports.

open_questions: Do these competing criteria — feedback improvement, workflow prediction, outline quality — converge into one benchmark, or stay fragmented?
Does outline-first generation (ScaffoldAgent) measurably beat report-first approaches on the multi-turn feedback test?
Will production stacks like Deep Agents + Bedrock AgentCore adopt any of these academic evaluation criteria?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you're building a deep research agent, decide up front which bar you're optimizing — feedback-driven report quality, personalized workflow prediction, or outline-driven long-form coherence — because they pull the design in different directions; the AWS Deep Agents + Bedrock AgentCore pattern gives you the isolated, multi-step execution plumbing regardless.

day_captions.b453c7e259c052f6: Turns to the report itself: ScaffoldAgent treats the outline as the optimization target, using utility-guided dynamic outline optimization for open-ended, multi-round-retrieval reports.
